taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Two accepted varieties are recognized: var. caespitosa and var. signata. The species-level learner preserves this distinction without assigning the Joey plant to variety.
look_here_first: Notice what is missing: there are no ray florets. Barbara's buttons makes a rounded button-like head of many tubular disc flowers. Then check the narrow leaves, hemispheric involucre, numerous paleae on the receptacle, and the persistent scale-like pappus on the cypselae.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora lists Marshallia caespitosa. Williamson — detailed county treatment documents M. caespitosa var. signata. Kerr — Kerr WMA flora documents M. caespitosa var. signata with voucher. Current Kew accepts both varieties under M. caespitosa.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Species-level PASS; the Joey developing-head frame does not establish variety.

best_field_traits: perennial herb with narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate leaves
heads discoid rather than radiate — no petal-like ray florets
showy rounded/button-like head containing many bisexual tubular florets
hemispheric involucre with several close series of narrow phyllaries
receptacle with conspicuous paleae/bractlets among flowers
five fused stamens per floret forming an anther cylinder
inferior ovary becoming a strongly ribbed cypsela
morphology_keys.family_training: Useful Asteraceae exception card: a showy composite head can be entirely disc florets and still be Asteraceae.
morphology_keys.video_training: Joey's frame shows developing button-like capitula in local limestone habitat before full bloom.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the large rounded button head, absence of ray florets, narrow leaves, involucre/paleae and pappus rather than flower color.
